candidates.title: The First Known Computer Algorithm Was Published With Literary Footnotes Longer Than the Paper Itself
candidates.fact: In 1843, Ada Lovelace translated Luigi Menabrea's French article on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine and appended seven 'Notes' labeled A through G. Her footnotes were nearly three times longer than the original engineering paper and contained Note G, the first published algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers.
candidates.context: Lovelace called her approach 'poetical science', blending mathematical logic with literary imagination. She also predicted that computing machines could one day compose music and manipulate symbols beyond pure arithmetic.
